chunks: And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled concerning a man who made a bequest to another while the one for whom the bequest was made was absent, and then the one to whom the bequest had been made died before the testator. He عليه السلام said: "The bequest belongs to the heir of the one to whom it was made."

And he عليه السلام said: "Whoever makes a bequest to someone, whether present or absent, and the beneficiary dies before the testator, then the bequest belongs to the heir of the one to whom it was made, unless he retracts his bequest before he dies."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: made a bequest or testamentary assignment
key_terms.الْمُوصَى لَهُ: the beneficiary to whom the bequest was made
key_terms.الْمُوصِي: the testator who made the bequest

ai.seo_question: If the beneficiary of a bequest dies before the testator, does the bequest go to the beneficiary’s heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on bequests: if a beneficiary dies before the testator, the bequest transfers to the beneficiary’s heir. The ruling applies whether the beneficiary was present or absent, unless the testator revokes the bequest before his own death.
